questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important to study in a European city, and preferably a capital or big city. Budapest was not my top priority but ended up being perfect for me. It was also a big plus, that it was a bit cheaper to live in than some of the other cities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Before leaving for Budapest it was a bit hard to find out who to contact from the university in Budapest with questions and I did not know which courses I was going to take, when I arrived because the application process for courses opened a bit late in my opinion, and a lot of the courses I got pre-approved did not get created in the end. Therefore I had to redo almost all of the administrative work I had done before arriving and had to spend  a significant amount of time getting a proper overlook and finding the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host univeristy in Budapest was not the best at replying to mails, before I got there. They were closed for summer-break 2 weeks in August, where everything needed to fall into place, before leaving, which stressed me out a bit. Once their break ended, it was necessary for me to call them a couple of times, and they seemed a bit stressed out and annoyed with this. This can maybe have something to do with the fact that they told the students upon arrival, that they had been understaffed. Once I got to Budapest, however, they were really nice and helpful, had gotten another staff-member for the Erasmus-students, and everything fell into place

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Once I got to Budapest, everything got sorted out with the assistance from the host university and also the very helpful assistance from KU. So my advice would be to, of course have all your documents, pre-approvals and applications filled out and sent to the respective parties, but most of it had to be re-done when I got there, so try not to stress too much about this stuff beforehand

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: On Whatsapp there were created different chatgroups for the incoming Erasmus students in Budapest. I actually first found the housing I ended up living in, once I was in Budapest, because I desperately needed to move out of the room I had been assigned before departure (read below in additional comments). One of the chatgroups on Whatsapp was called "housing", and in that a girl texted that she was in the same situation as me and had found an apartment for which she needed someone to rent the other rooms. She had found the apartment through a person she met at the host university who rented an apartment from the same landlord. So in that sense, it was fairly easy to find housing, even when I was in the city

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A lot of the students I met on exchange had found housing through "United Erasmus Housing", which they seemed satisfied with, so I would recommend looking into that. Also I would recommend joining the Whatsapp "housing" group where I could see that several people found housing through, but I think this was more last-minute than the United Erasmus Housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Before leaving for Budapest I had gotten assigned a room in a dormitory through ELTE (the host university). The room was shared with one other person i did not know beforehand and was a bit outside of the city, on the Buda side. Once I got there, I unfortunately discovered that the dormitory, and the room, was in very bad condition. There was one very small kitchen in the hallway, that had to be shared with a lot of people and there was very dirty, the appliances were moldy and broken, and there were bugs everywhere. I quickly moved out of the room and found housing on my own. I would not recommend living in the dormitories, which is why I chose "1" above.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Look above in the "orientation and asistance upon arrival" field.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to send mails to both the university, that had a mail address for incoming Erasmus students and call them, even though you have to search a bit to find the phone numbers. Once I was in Budapest I ended up having to text some of the specific professors teaching the different courses I wanted to register for, as it was up to them to decide if I could take their courses as some of these were masters-courses, and they seem a be a bit strict about only accepting master students for the master courses in the beginning. Once I e-mailed the professors however, these would most of the time let me attend the course with a few exceptions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly succesful I would say. As beforementioned some of the courses I originally got preregistered ended up not being created and it seemed like I would not be able to register for some of the ones I needed to cover for my obligatory course at home as these were masters courses, so for a while I was worried that I would not be able to take enough ECTS-credits at the host university to cover for this. But it ended up working out, and I got most of the courses I wanted and needed by texting the specific professors. Fortunately, ELTE offers many courses in the same fields, I think, so it should be possible to find something in your field

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be persistent in telling the respective parties about which courses you need to take. Then they will be helpful in making sure, you can get enough credits in my experience

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Read above

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching was noticeably different from that of UCPH and the academic level was lower. The courses are a lot less ECTS-credits, so I took courses with 2, 3 or 4 ECTS meaning that you have to take more courses than at UCPH. I did not find the content of the courses as challenging as UCPH - for me the hardest part was organising all the courses and getting an overlook of the demands and requirements of each of the courses, as some of these had exams, some did not, some you were only allowed to miss a few times, and some did not keep attendance at all, and some had assignments every week, while others did not. 
For me the reading burden was very low compared to UCPH, and for some of the courses it was not required to read anything. I had to do a lot of assignments through the semester though. 
For me, the facilities were not as great as those of UCPH in my opinion. There were no auditoriums and no real places to sit and study, which I missed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Human Memory across the Lifespan
- Cognitive Psychology 2
- Cognitive/Affective Neuropsychology
- Cognitive/Affective Neuroscience
- Crisis, Crossroads, Trauma and Resilience in Films
- Hungarian Culture: Narratives of Freedom and Oppression
- Psychological Ethics and Legal Issues
- Psychology and Crime
- Psychology and Crime - Case studies

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the "psychology and crime - case studies" and found it very interesting. Also the "cognitive psychology 2" had some nice topics on the syllabus. The professors of the different courses I attended were mostly really nice and passionate about their subjects, which was inspiring to me

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The utilities in my housing ended up being much more expensive that the price (50 euros) we payed each month beforehand. This was the case for many of the people I met there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than I thought - pretty much the same as in Denmark. Going out to eat and drink was cheap in my experience. Transportation was really cheap - with the student discount, you could get a monthly past for all of Hungary for only 40 dkk.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really use the clubs at the host institution. It was possible to sign up for sports through ELTE, and I signed up for a weekly badminton course at first. I went there once and the teacher could only speak hungarian and did not instruct at all, so I dropped the course

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I actually do not know. ESN (Erasmus Social Network) and ELB (Erasmus Life Budapest), which were 2 organisations for Erasmus students were however, really good at organising parties and events, and I attended a lot of these and found them really nice

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend attending the ELB events, because these are fun and a great opportunity to meet new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are very good opportunities for going out to eat or drink, so I would recommend taking advantage of that. The historical sights were really impressive

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the ELB events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The attitude of hungarian people towards foreigners was not always the nicest and some did not speak english

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The city was beautiful and there were a lot of things to do

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be patient and positive about the application and registration process - it will get sorted out in the end
2. Budapest has a lot to offer in regards to going out, the nightlife and the cultural sights - take advantage of it
3. I only met 2 other danish people in the whole semester. But it did not matter actually - my advice is to be open and take it as an opportunity to meet interesting people and learn about other countries and cultures

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I have covered all of it in the other fields

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience actually. It was very nice to experience how everything works at other universities, I met a lot of nice people and enjoyed living in Budapest a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Of course it can be tough being away at times, but it was definitely worth it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
